category_title: Highly reserved and anxious students with significant writing avoidance
minimal_context: The student is sitting with a blank sheet of paper during independent writing time in the writing workshop.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our writing workshop. Please start your independent writing on your blank sheet of paper.

STUDENT: (Sits staring at the blank sheet of paper with a worried look, almost a scowl. Writes a word or two and then erases them.)

TUTOR: You need to keep writing. What do you think you should write next?

STUDENT: (Turns her head away and shrinks in her seat, not speaking a word.)

TUTOR: Let me help you get started. (Approaches and touches her on the shoulder)

STUDENT: (Moans with apparent anxiety, turns her head, and shrinks further in her seat.)

options.A: Require three revisions per independent writing assignment during the workshop and only grade the final (third) draft.
options.B: Provide a choice of a weekly writing workshop timetable stuck to the desk or a booklet of daily timetables.
options.C: Consult with previous teachers, parents, and specialists; leverage the student's existing strengths (reading) to bridge into social and academic growth.
options.D: Provide flexibility, particularly with timelines, by giving the student extra time to complete independent writing assignments during the workshop.
